short: A receivable you have accepted will not be collected.
seoTitle: Bad Debt — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: A bad debt is an amount owed by a customer that the business has accepted will not be recovered. Writing them off is painful once and honest thereafter.
definition: A bad debt is an amount owed by a customer that the business has accepted will not be recovered. It is written off against profit, removing the receivable from the balance sheet.
bodyHtml:
Why Bad Debt matters

Carrying uncollectable invoices overstates assets and profit at the same time. Writing them off is painful once and honest thereafter.

Bad Debt formula

Bad debt % = Bad debts written off ÷ Credit sales × 100

Rising ratios point at credit policy, not just at difficult customers.

How Bad Debt works in practice

Set a policy — for example, provide against anything past 180 days and write off past a year unless recovery is genuinely in progress. Every write-off is also feedback about the credit decision that created it.

faq.question: When should I write off a bad debt?
faq.answer: When recovery efforts have realistically ended. Until then, a provision is the better treatment.

faq.question: Can GST be recovered on a bad debt?
faq.answer: GST law does not generally provide for reversal of tax on bad debts, which is why credit control matters more, not less.
